newsitem.title: USA: USDA seeks public comment on interstate meat issue.
newsitem.headline: USDA seeks public comment on interstate meat issue.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Tuesday said it was seeking public comment on whether to change federal meat inspection laws to allow interstate shipment of state-inspected meat and poultry.

In a notice in the Federal Register, USDA also rescheduled one of the public hearings it will hold on the long-running issue this summer. The department said there will be a meeting in Washington, D.C., on July 22 instead of June 19 as previously scheduled.
USDA will also hold meetings June 16-17 in Sioux Falls, South Dakota. It said written comments will be accepted and made a part of the proceedings through August 22.
Currently, only federally-inspected meat and poultry may be sold across state lines.

Some state-inspected meat companies have been pressing USDA to allow them to sell their products in other states without federal inspection. They argue that federal law already requires all state meat and poultry inspection programs to be "at least equal" to federal standards.
Twenty-six states operate their own inspection programs.
